name: Deficit Push-Up
description: The deficit push-up is performed with the hands elevated on platforms, blocks, or dumbbells, allowing the chest to descend below the level of the hands for a deeper range of motion than a standard push-up. This extended stretch under load increases time under tension and pectoral recruitment, making it a more demanding bodyweight pressing variation.

execution.starting_position: Place hands on two elevated platforms (push-up handles, dumbbells, or sturdy blocks) slightly wider than shoulder width. Assume a push-up position with straight body alignment.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the platforms at an equal height between 4 and 6 inches. Ensure they are stable and will not slide on the surface.
steps: Step 1: Begin in a high plank position with hands on the platforms, body in a straight line.
Step 2: Lower the chest between and below the platforms by bending the elbows to roughly 45 degrees.
Step 3: Continue lowering until the chest is below the level of the hands, feeling a deep stretch.
Step 4: Press powerfully upward through the palms, extending the elbows fully at the top.
Step 5: Maintain a rigid plank body position from head to heels throughout.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale as you lower the chest toward the floor. Exhale forcefully as you push back up.
common_mistakes: Allowing the hips to sag downward on the descent
Not descending low enough to benefit from the deficit
Flaring the elbows to 90 degrees, increasing shoulder stress
safety_considerations: Ensure the platforms are on a non-slip surface
Only perform this variation if you can complete standard push-ups with solid form
Avoid if you have shoulder instability or rotator cuff issues
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Descend until the chest drops 2–4 inches below the hand level for a meaningful deficit. Full elbow extension at the top.
coaching_cues: Chest drops below the hands — that's the whole point
Keep the body rigid from heels to crown
Press hard through the platforms on the way up
